a987283dd4fe: Ask: «Mountains or sea?» and let the student answer however they can. Then: «Now we'll learn to say it naturally in Polish.»
1fb352c6e308: After each row, ask the learner one question: «A ty, co uwielbiasz?». On the last row stress: negation → dopełniacz (genitive).
7d77ca7f5668: Reveal column by column and ask at once: «Co woli twoja mama? Co wolą twoje dzieci / przyjaciele?».
58c9f49488ff: After the formula — a quick round: «kawa czy herbata, kot czy pies, lato czy zima?». The student answers only in a full sentence with niż.
9210d239f59d: Both options are correct with nouns; «od» is slightly more bookish. Ask the student to translate one sentence in two ways.
29db6cf3cb50: Ask: «Na czym grasz? W co grasz? Czym się interesujesz?». For «grać na» add: na komputerze, na konsoli.
d1b0b29cfc5f: Most mistakes here come from translating English “to” as one preposition: Polish chooses between do and na. Ask the student to name 5 places they go this week, with the correct preposition.
d09355c573fe: Explain with the questions: “na czym?” — what I travel on; “po co?” — the purpose of the trip. Both sentences are correct.
d7d748ebb4cf: Say each trap in English first and let the student translate it themselves — only then reveal the correct version.
df06b94d94f0: «Odwiedzam» is a very persistent calque; listen out for it until the end of the lesson.
